column1: # The audit check-off -- one row per finding, authored.
# Rendered into spec/AUDIT.md by tools/emit-findings-register.sh; the state is edited here.
# Columns: id, alias, section, state, title, evidence, owes, laws
# `laws` (optional, and required on an open row): the law this finding is an instance of, as its
# `number`+`clause` in `spec/laws.tsv` (`51b`, `14a`), a comma-separated list of them, or
# `candidate:<slug>` for a finding that *proposes* a law rather than instantiating one. A row without
# the cell is *unclassified*: the emitter prints that count every run and refuses to let it grow.
#   todo         outstanding; `owes` says what would close it, and an empty cell is a defect
#   in progress  being worked on now; `owes` says by whom and since when
#   done         settled: fixed, assessed faithful, a deliberate deviation, or refuted
# `section` is the `## N.` pass in spec/audit/passes.md that carries the full account.
# `alias` is an id this finding was also known by; a citation to either resolves here.

law 25's declared witness cannot fail when the block path's validation gate is switched off. **Both halves are now settled, and the `owes` cell's remedy turned out not to be dischargeable as written.** The second half — "the switch from scheduler mode to validation flag is covered by no test" — is closed: `law24_the_effect_mode_is_what_enables_the_certificate` observes the behaviour the wiring controls (a claim on a channel whose newest write is DFS-later is refused under `RelaxedValidated` and accepted under every other mode), where replacing the wiring with `false` had left every test green. The first half was attacked by *searching* for the divergence the remedy asks for: **seventeen hand-written shapes, including the ordering law 24 exists for** (a produce `o`, a consume `p` and a second produce `q` with `o < p < q` in DFS order, where `q` writes `p`'s channel — the DFS-later write the certificate refuses at the queue level), run under `EffectMode::Relaxed`, **which has no certificate at all**, at 40 repetitions each against the sequential reference. **None diverged on state hash or event count.** The reason is structural rather than a weak search: `Relaxed` preserves *per-channel* DFS op order in the claim queue (law 20) and frees only cross-channel interleaving, which changes neither how many events commit nor what the space holds for any program of this class — the certificate's observable effect is at the acquire, not on the resulting state. So `law25_...` cannot be made to fail by deleting the gate, not because its strategy is too narrow but because no state-level divergence exists to witness. **What would close it more strongly than a test**: a proof that relaxed ≡ sequential on state for the scheduler's fragment, which is a modelling obligation rather than a witness

the other half of the ingress->validate->process pipeline is still unbounded: `mpsc::unbounded_channel()` at `node/src/runtime/node_runtime.rs:758` carries full `BlockMessage`s, with a second unbounded tap at `:2604`. R15 bounded the processor-input half of this same pipeline (`:764-781`) and this half was missed — the shape the register records as this port's most-repeated defect. It is the one candidate mechanism for #117 the audit could not rule out, because its depth is measured by nothing The **observation half landed** in #120 — a queue observer at the validated, autopropose and attestation stages — so the depth is readable for the first time; the bound is still outstanding, which is why `tools/check-bounded-ingress-queues.sh` remains red. **The observable has been used, and it strikes this queue as #117's mechanism:** on the frozen reproduction the depth reads 0.0 at every sample on all three nodes while anon climbs 30 MiB -> 4 GiB and all three are OOM-killed (2026-10-01, `measure/c175-queue-depth`, configuration in the artifact header). The queue is empty throughout the ramp, and a drained queue cannot retain what the measurement found retained. **Bounded 2026-10-01**: `mpsc::channel(MAX_VALIDATED_BLOCKS)` at `node_runtime.rs:771` and `:2667` (the validated-blocks queue and the autopropose/attestation tap beside it), with the send at each producer awaiting, and **the type carries the bound** - `wire_block_processing` and `wire_block_processing_observed` now return `mpsc::Sender<BlockMessage>` for that half, and `block_processor::apply` takes one, so a caller cannot reach an unbounded path without changing a signature. `tools/check-bounded-ingress-queues.sh --gate` is green and runs in the lint job. The bound is a **policy** number and the row says so: the observer read depth 0.0 at every sample on the frozen reproduction, so 1024 is the depth the processor input beside it uses, not a measured envelope. The falsifier is `a_bounded_queue_makes_its_producer_wait`, which fails when the capacity is widened (observed red at 16) because a queue that never makes its producer wait is bounded in name only; the pipeline's own liveness is a devnet run with both taps live.

a measurement's artifacts cannot say what they measured: the devnet's arm samplers write no configuration column, so six arm files carry only a filename and one of them holds two different runs; a killed node's cgroup is gone, so a peak read through `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` returns 0 for exactly the nodes a death measurement exists to observe (`acceptance.log:746-747`); and `docs/src/node/validator-requirements.md:120-121` states a figure its own artifact refutes — "29 regions of exactly 64 MiB ... fully resident" where the snapshot holds 29 regions of exactly 32 MiB (5.7 MiB resident between them) and 11 of exactly 64 MiB, which are the arena heaps **Closed 2026-10-01**: the three parts are addressed by work that already exists — the current samplers echo their configuration into each artifact's header (`n149-sweep-run.sh` writes `tree`/`image`/`sweep`/`windows` lines), the Stage A sampler (`n117-after-fix-run.sh`) resolves the cgroup from the container id (`docker inspect` → `State.Pid` → `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`) and reads the peak while the node lives — the fix §27 itself names — and `docs/src/node/validator-requirements.md:141-150` now states the measured histogram (29 × 32 MiB worker stacks + 11 × 64 MiB arena heaps).

the merge's rejection search carried the rejected set as *state* beside the accepted set, and it is not state: after every step `rejected = union{conflicts(x) : x in accepted}`, so a state is fully described by the accepted set alone. Carrying the second set made a state reachable by one queue entry per ordering that reaches it, cloning two `BTreeSet`s per push - 19,728,200 queue entries to expand 2,046 states on a 20-chain fork, a ratio factorial in the branch width. Those clones are 97 % of the live heap of a node at its cgroup ceiling (#117), grown 343 -> 1488 MiB within one run. Fixed by carrying the accepted set alone, which expands each state once (20 chains: 11.3 s -> 13.4 ms)

the enumeration behind C177 expands one state per nonempty subset of chains that induces an acyclic subgraph, which is `2^n - 1` when the chains do not conflict and `2^(p+1) - 2` on a fork - exponential in the width of a merge scope, unrelated to how many rejection options come out (40 chains: 2^21 states / 34.6 s, infeasible before C177). Fixed for the case the precondition covers - a relation symmetric and irreflexive on its keys makes reachable exactly independent-set and terminal exactly dominating, so the terminal states are the maximal independent sets and Bron-Kerbosch enumerates those, 40 chains 2^21 states -> 60 states, counts now linear in width. **But the node's real input is directed**: 3 attempts of the frozen reproduction, 9 node-runs, every one asymmetric (376-653 pairs among keys), because `resolve_conflict_set` unions each key's dependencies into its conflict set. The rewrite therefore declines on the node and it still expands up to 1,663,395 states per merge at the 33-43 chain widths it reaches, roughly doubling per chain (50 chains would be ~5e10) - the node is running on the C177 dedup alone, and is one wider fork from the same ceiling. The precondition had been checked on 2-chain merge fixtures with an empty final set, which cannot exhibit a dependency-induced asymmetry **Fixed 2026-10-01** (`spec/audit/evidence/n127-loaded-results.md`, `n127-directed-results.md`): the directed path quotients its states by the **rejected set**, which is the value the search returns, so every accepted set sharing a rejection union is one state and the counted work is bounded by the output - measured on a live fork, 161-174 chains expanded **153-290** states against the pre-quotient tree's **650,159** at 29 chains, and 31-45 MiB against 647-689 MiB while carrying the wider DAG. The gate was observed red with the quotient disabled: 16,383 states for one option at 14 keys, where the fixed tree expands 14. The exactness is not taken on trust - the option set is identical, so no block hash moves.

the retention falsifier measured its peak with a thread that starves, so on CI it reported an impossible value: `kept 58564 KiB` against `grew 40080 KiB`, i.e. more kept than was ever grown, while jemalloc's own closing stats said `retained: 0` - the purge the test exists to check was working and the instrument was not. A 5 ms polling thread against 16 churn threads on a small runner never gets scheduled, so its 'peak' is a baseline reading taken later and the two assertions built on it (growth budget, retention ratio) fail on a machine's scheduling rather than on the memory. It also made the branch CI-red for two commits with the *tests* never running behind it. Fixed by sampling inside the churn threads, which cannot starve, every tenth iteration. **And the same class one layer down**: the 1.5 s settle sleep before the retained read is also a machine constant - the purge is done by the allocator's background thread, and after sixteen churn threads it takes longer to become visible in `Anonymous` on CI (77 % retained) than here (29 %), which fails an assertion about an allocator that is working (`stats.retained` reads 0). Now polls until the value stops falling, capped at 30 s. **The file also had two tests where its own header says it must have one**: libtest runs them in parallel, so each one's process-wide `Anonymous` baseline absorbed the other's churn - measured here, `grew 12056 KiB` in parallel against 6560 KiB alone, and worse and less predictably so on a small runner. Now one churn in one test, asserting both properties from that single measurement. **And the retention ratio is reported, not gated**: it was the acceptance criterion for the purge configuration (purged ~31 %, un-purged ~100 %), and it reads 29 % here against a reproducible **76-77 % on CI while jemalloc's own `retained` counter reads 0 in the same run** - the allocator reporting no retention while a gate built on it fails, which means the gate is measuring the machine
column7: the ratio is the open question and is deliberately not gated: `Anonymous` on CI stays at ~76 % of the churn's growth after an adaptive settle while `stats.retained` reads 0, so what holds those pages there is unmeasured. Either find it (arenas, per-thread caches, and the metadata that scales with the core count are the candidates) or state the `Anonymous` ratio as machine-calibrated and leave the configuration claim to the node-side shim, which reads jemalloc's own counters

column5: the class the register has no law for: work whose cost grows with an input nothing bounds, with the guard - where one exists - applied *after* the cost rather than before it. Three symptoms, each tracked separately with its own slug or with an unrelated law: the merge's conflict search expands one state per acyclic subset of the conflict relation (2^n - 1 where chains do not conflict, 2^(p+1) - 2 on a fork) and the node's relation is directed (376-653 asymmetric pairs among keys, from `with_dependencies`), so the fast path declines and up to 1,663,395 states are expanded on a single merge - which is C178; the ingress pipeline's second half is an unbounded channel (C175, `candidate:bounded-queue-depth`); and a 3.2k-block start-up rebuild measured ~1.8 GB and ~17 minutes before the API opened (#68, `candidate:startup-rebuild-envelope`). Closed #85 is the same shape in its sharpest form: the matcher enumerates 2^n subsets *before* the bound that refuses them **Closed 2026-10-01: the class is Law 55** (`spec/Rchain/Bounded.lean`, `proved-model`). Clause a is *the guard is before the work* - `the_work_never_exceeds_the_budget`, an invariant over `Reach`, with the defect's own shape in the same model (`the_late_guard_overspends`) so that the two are relations and not a schedule that happened to behave. Clause b is *the bound cannot change an answer* - `a_larger_budget_does_not_change_an_answer` and `a_spent_budget_carries_no_answer`, which is what makes a bound a resource policy rather than a fork (Law 17). **The members it asked for are held**: the merge search bounded by its output (C178, gated and measured - 161-174 chains expanding 153-290 states against the pre-quotient tree's 650,159 at 29), and the ingress queue bound (C175). The third, the start-up envelope (#68), is where C189 is: its measurement does not reproduce on the current build, which is a fact about the rig rather than about this row. The `candidate:` slug this row filed is **promoted rather than deleted** - Law 55's own note names it

the other half of the LFS sync defect has no row and no longer has an issue: a failed sync attempt latches (`start_requester` consumed by the first *started* attempt and never re-armed; the attempt `take`s the importer and both receivers with no inverse), so the node sits in `NodeSyncing` for good with a serving API and no error line. #102 diagnosed it and was closed into #125 (the `Terminal` cause), and the candidate that issue carried -- `candidate:lfs-sync-recovery` -- lived only in its prose, so it is filed here rather than deleted with the issue. **Fixed 2026-10-01**: the retry is a loop inside the spawned task with the importer and both receivers borrowed by `&mut` (they have no inverse — the engine holds only the senders, so a re-armed trigger was never implementable), fed by a **shared latest-fringe slot** that now keeps *every* bootstrap answer instead of discarding later ones in silence, and bounded by `MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS`; the bound ends in a **terminal signal** — a new handle, deliberately not `finished`, which `node_launch` selects on to stop the node, because a `finished` here would take it into `NodeRunning` on a DAG it never populated

the merge's shape is observable only as process maxima, not as a distribution: `search_census` publishes MERGES, MAX_KEYS, MAX_CONFLICTS, MAX_ASYMMETRIC and MAX_EXPANDED plus one log line every five seconds, which says how bad the *worst* merge was and nothing about how often. The two numbers a bound on this class needs - Stage 2's threshold N and Stage 3's fee schedule (#127's change record) - have no data to be set from, because a maximum is not a distribution **Closed 2026-10-01 by derivation rather than measurement** (#153 closed on this): the bound landed as C191 and cannot bind a bonded network - `max-number-of-parents` defaults to 255 against a shipped `number-of-active-validators` of 100 (2.55x), and the parent set is the round snapshot, one message per sender - so there is no distribution from which to read a threshold, and #153's own condition allowed "a measurement or a derivation". The instrument the row also owed was fixed in its own earlier commit (the shape metrics carry their own bucket ranges, with a regression test asserting they reach the observed values).

a validator that speaks and then stops caps the fringe at the height it stopped at: its last message stays in `latest_msgs` for ever (`block-storage/src/dag/message_state.rs:90-102`, one entry per sender, no bond check, no eviction), so every later candidate still justifies it while `LIVENESS_WINDOW` (5) has already dropped it from the live partition -- and `check_min_messages` then compares a four-message set against a three-sender partition by size as well as by coverage, returns `NoAdvance::Coverage`, and the fringe never advances again. This is #70's second stop, and it is why finality moved +4 heights and then pinned in two independent runs (40 -> 44 on the 2026-09-29 testnet, 14 -> 18 in the campaign's attempt 2) with `LIVENESS_WINDOW` = 5. C174 narrowed the partition to the live weight set and left this side of it standing. The fixture could not see it because its silent validator *never speaks*; the case a real net produces is 'spoke, then stopped'

the merge search was unbounded **at the site that spends the work**: `computeRejectionOptions` enumerates one state per nonempty subset that induces an acyclic subgraph with nothing refusing it before it runs, so a 33-43 chain scope costs up to 2,026,511 steps on record (nine node-runs) and the enumerated worst case is 2^43 = 8.8e12 -- the class C180 names, work whose cost grows with an input nothing bounds. **Why not a threshold on scope width**, which is what the change order proposed: width does not predict the cost (43 chains -> 899,236 states against 35 -> 1,663,395; nine runs at 30-37 chains -> 389,977 / 442,202 / 985,391 / 1,726,295 / 2,026,511), and the scope is node-relative -- `interpreter_util.rs:265-277` filters the parent set by the local DAG, so two nodes can disagree on whether a block exceeds N, and a `block_summary` refusal runs through `mark_failed_attributable`, which nothing clears, so a threshold there would manufacture the C173 wedge. The bound is applied where the work is counted (`SearchCensus::expanded`) and refuses **by dropping the merge locally**: the error reaches `ValidateError::Internal` (`multi_parent_casper.rs:361`), which inserts no metadata, so no block is recorded failed and no node is estranged. Two properties are asserted rather than argued: an exceeded search carries **no answer** (a truncated option set would pick a different rejection -- law 17a -- so it is discarded, never returned), and a budget that is not hit returns the identical option set. The guard was observed red by disabling the bound checks. The number is provisional: ~5x the largest merge on record, to be re-read from a campaign on C171's arm

the second stop of #70 was **the parent set the node's own proposer built**, and it is fixed in the proposer rather than in the rule: `create_msg_and_update_sender` set every block's height to `max(latest_msgs) + 1` and justified **every** `latest_msgs` entry, and `calculate_next_fringe_support_map` derives each candidate's `seen_by` from `parents \u2216 next_layer` — so a parent set that *is* every sender's newest message has almost no remainder, the head of each round has an empty one and the later movers have seen a prefix, and no candidate is a full partition. Measured through the production entry point with three live validators at the devnet's `100/100/50`, no kill and no stopped validator: `Support { supporting: 0, total: 250, full_partitions: 0, candidates: 2 }` — `supporting: 0` is not a shortfall, the numerator is zero before the quorum is consulted. **The `150 of 250` the devnet logged is this defect's half-fixed shape**, produced on the way to the correction and reproduced in-process. The fix is the round snapshot: `DagMessageState::round_parents` holds the `latest_msgs` as of the last round boundary — the first message at which every bonded sender has advanced past the previous one, with a sender silent past `LIVENESS_WINDOW` retired so the boundary cannot freeze — and the proposer justifies that. Heights stay `max + 1`, no validity rule and no gate changes, and the same chain now publishes a fringe, tracking the tip at a constant 12-height lag (48/60, 168/180, 348/360). This file's own header had said since it was written that a lockstep DAG 'never finalizes' and that the Scala round-robin spec is `ignore`d for it; three devnet runs and a fixed derivation went into chasing a gate whose input the node never produced. Both earlier readings in this row were wrong: the pin is not the kill (14 of 16 survivor node-runs had finished finalising before it) and `150 = 100 + 50` is not the departed validator's stake (10 of the instrumented run's `150 of 250` lines are pre-kill).

**a parent set that is the justification set *is* the block creator's arithmetic, and a fixture that supplies its own counters cannot see it.** `block_creator.rs:58-75` derives both the new block's `block_num` and its `seq_num` **from the parent set** — `max(justifications.block_num) + 1` and `justifications.find(sender).seq_num + 1` — so any proposer whose parents no longer carry its own newest message reuses its `(sender, seq_num)`, and the DAG refuses the block, correctly, as an equivocation: `ERROR Self-created block #93 (seq 92) failed validation with internal error: failed to insert block into DAG: equivocation detected: sender produced two blocks with the same sequence number`, after which autopropose halts (`consecutive_failures` >= 3 breaks the timer in `node_runtime.rs:1504`) and the chain produces nothing while work is available. Found on the node, not by the tests: the round-snapshot fix's first version omitted the proposer's own entry, every fixture in `casper/tests/finalization.rs` passed its `sender_seq` explicitly, and `create_msg_and_update_sender` takes its `seq_num` from `latest_msgs` rather than from the parent set — so three fixtures and a policy comparison all agreed the chain was linked while the node disagreed. Fixed by `parents_for_new_block(sender)`, which replaces the sender's own entry in the round snapshot with its newest message; the first block of a round is unaffected because the sender's newest *is* the snapshot's entry, so the cross-sender snapshot the gate needs is untouched. **And the fixture can see it now**: `a_validator_proposing_twice_in_one_round_keeps_its_sequence` derives its numbers from the parent set the way the block creator does and proposes twice from one validator inside a round — observed red with the substitution disabled, failing with the node's own sentence. The general form is the one worth keeping: **a fixture that owns the counter it is testing cannot test the rule that computes it.**

**the round snapshot and the block creator's derived numbers are load-bearing against each other, and three repairs have now been ruled out by measurement.** The gate needs a candidate's parents to reach *beyond* the next layer, which is what the cross-sender snapshot gives and what `latest_msgs` never did (the pin: finality 15-61 heights behind, last advancing 87-104 s before the kill). The block creator needs the parent set to contain the proposer's **own newest message**, because `block_creator.rs:58-75` derives `block_num` and `seq_num` **from that set**. Both cannot hold. Ruled out, each measured rather than argued: (1) **pure snapshot** — the pin is fixed and verified twice on the node (finality 3-4 behind, 87 of 91, 90 of 94, 105 of 109), but a second proposal in a round reuses the proposer's `(sender, seq_num)` and the DAG refuses it as an equivocation, three of which halt autopropose; (2) **refuse the second proposal** (`has_advanced_past_the_round`) — zero equivocations on the node and the pin still fixed, but it **deadlocks**: the round closes only when every bonded sender has advanced, a quiet sender stops holding it back only once `LIVENESS_WINDOW` heights pass above its last message, and that is measured from the tip the refusal freezes, so a validator killed inside the window is never retired (in-process: the tip goes 1 -> 2 over thirty-seven further rounds of attempts, then nothing); (3) **replace the sender's own entry with its newest for that one proposal** (the escape, local, no clock) — the deadlock goes and the in-process falsifier runs green, but the equivocation **returns** (7 on one node, each at seq 3) and finality degrades to a 27-height gap, because the proposal rate far exceeds the round rate so most proposals become escapes. **What is not yet tried, and the next question to answer:** stop deriving `block_num` and `seq_num` from the justification set at all and take them from `latest_msgs[sender]`, which dissolves the tension if validators do not check those numbers against the justifications — a question `casper/src/validate.rs` and `spec/RChain/Casper/Dag.lean` answer, not a devnet.

a node that LFS-syncs a **mature** chain cannot replay its own restored blocks, and never catches up: `populate_dag` inserts every non-genesis restored block as `BlockMetadata::from_block`, and the `fringe`/`fringe_state_hash` a replay needs are a **local recomputation** produced by validation — not block fields, not on the wire. So the node's `fringe_states` cache holds `fringe_hash_of(∅) → 0` and never the chain's real fringe key, and every block whose `close_block` anchors the epoch seed to the fringe state replays to a different post-state. Reproduced on a live devnet, 2 of 2 attempts: the joiner synced to 27 and 23 and stayed there while the bootstrap ran to 127 and 123, logging 93 and 92 `regenerated mergeable channels for block <a> but replay computed <b> instead of <c>` errors naming the **epoch-boundary** close deploy (#139)

**the memory ceiling the class is about no longer reproduces on the current build**, so the falsifier that was supposed to decide it cannot fire: the controlled baseline at 8 GiB crosses **0 of 3** nodes on the pre-quotient tree *and* on the fixed tree, even under the census rig's own load (four deploys at T+30, `stop 2` at T+120) - peaks 647-689 MiB against a 3000 MiB threshold, while the widest merge scope is 29 chains pre-quotient and 161-174 after. The ramp #117 was filed about needed a DAG shape the proposer fix moved (#138), so 'the ramp is gone' is not a testable claim on this host: the merge's counted cost is now 2,000x lower where the two trees can be compared, and the ramp's remaining mechanism, if it exists on the current lineage, is unnamed
column7: **#154 took the second exit, 2026-10-01 — a re-scope, not a new rig.** Two pre-registered rounds measured **0 of 3** crossings on the control *and* the fixed arm (`n127-directed-results.md`), and **0 of 3** under load with the fixed arm peaking 31-45 MiB against the control's 647-689 (`n127-loaded-results.md`). The first exit is not merely unmet but unreachable with these rigs: the input the ramp needs - the 32-43 chain scopes - was a DAG shape the proposer fix (#138) moved, and the widest scope on this lineage is 9 chains. So #117's and #68's memory claims are recorded as **unreproduced on the current lineage**, and the sizing point at `docs/src/node/validator-requirements.md:92` now says so - it no longer carries a figure to size from, and it does not claim the ramp is fixed. Account: passes §46.

column5: **a `validation_failed` record occupies a `(sender, seq_num)` the proposer's own arithmetic cannot see, so the node refuses its own next block as an equivocation** - the second and distinct mismatch of the pair C186 fixed. The H-1 gate scans **`msg_map`** (`casper/src/dag.rs:335`: any stored message carrying that `(sender, seq_num)` refuses the block before any partial write), while `block_creator.rs:71` derives `seq_num` from its **parent set**, which is the round snapshot built from `latest_msgs` - and `insert_msg_without_latest_mut` (`block-storage/src/dag/message_state.rs:284`) is the one writer that touches `msg_map` and not `latest_msgs`, by design (H-2: a failed block must not become a parent), reached from exactly one branch, `dag.rs`'s `validation_failed` arm. So a validator whose own block failed validation has spent a sequence number its proposal arithmetic cannot see, derives it again, and the DAG refuses the node's own block with C186's sentence; the **escaping** rule does not save it, because it reads `latest_msgs` too. Reproduced in process - `SeqNum(1)` on both sides - and **fixed 2026-10-01**: the proposer clears its own spent record before it derives a sequence number - `clear_own_failure_record` re-validates the node's own record that H-2 left out of `latest_msgs` and, on a pass, clears it through C193's `update_metadata`, which promotes the block back into the arithmetic; the result is deliberately ignored so a refusal stays a counted one rather than a silent decline. The structural assertion below still pins the disagreement - the fix clears the record, it does not change either structure. **Superseded as the *reachable* shape by C194**: the instrumented run (§48) found the sync produces no `validation failed` records, so this repair is defence for a genuine `Divergence` self-record while the self-equivocation actually seen is C194's race

**`max-number-of-parents` was read from configuration and consulted by no code in the tree**, so a block's justification set — the one block input a proposer chooses outright, and the input the merge is computed over — had no bound on either side: no proposer cap and no validation rule, while two doc comments (`proposer.rs`, `validate.rs`) and **C123's fix rationale** each asserted that it bounded exactly this set. The key's only sites were the field, the HOCON reader, the CLI arg, the mapper and the defaults; it is therefore also the **tenth member of C143's class** — parsed into `NodeConf` and read by nothing — which C143's own list of nine did not reach, and it takes the *other* horn of that register's disposition, enforcing the setting rather than refusing it, because unlike the keepalive and random-port knobs its documented purpose is one this port can honour. Fixed on both sides: `validate::justification_count` refuses a block above the bound, in `block_summary`'s pure list beside the F-3 bounds and threaded from `conf.casper.max_number_of_parents` exactly as `min_phlo_price` is, and `proposer.rs::create_block` refuses to build one rather than emit a block every validator will reject. The shipped default moves `2147483647 -> 255`, the protocol's existing per-block width (the `u8` seed index `MAX_BLOCK_DEPLOYS` already occupies, so the two per-block inputs share one bound) in `defaults.conf` and in the mirror fixture that proves the parsed defaults equal the documented ones; it is 2.55x the shipped `number-of-active-validators`, and the parent set is the round snapshot, one message per sender, so it binds no set a bonded network can produce. `0` or a negative value disables the check and a test asserts it, which is how a chain keeps the pre-#153 semantics exactly rather than by accident. **Hard fork (#51 category A)** and registered as one: a block justifying more parents than the bound is valid today and refused after, so an upgraded node rejects what an unupgraded one accepts. The reverse link is posted: the #51 §A row went up as issue comment 5937212825, on the second attempt — the first was refused by a permission classifier for the *form* of the call (a long inline heredoc body) rather than the action, and the same comment posted immediately from a body file. Worth knowing before concluding a refusal is about intent.

**attestation is bounded per remote *height*, and a round that comes to rest at one height is sealed by that same bound.** The attestation tap answers a remote block only if its height is strictly greater than the last height it answered (`attest_warranted`, `node_runtime.rs:2706`). On a net of three or more validators the peers react to the deploy-bearing block before any of them has produced, so every attestation in the round lands at the **same height**; every node's `last_attested_height` is then that height, no block above it exists or can now be produced, and the tap refuses every block that will ever arrive from a peer. With autopropose off nothing else requests a proposal, so no second round is enqueued and the proposer's own round veto and its bounded escape (`proposer.rs:531-547`) are never reached — the escape increments on a proposal *request*, and the tap is the only issuer here. The chain is sealed with its deploy unfinalised. Measured on the guard-live arm of the #149 sweep, 3 of 3 attempts at each of N in {3,5,8}: exactly N blocks after one deploy, all at a single height, and no finality at all; at N=2 the blocks arrive one at a time, each raises the tip before the other node answers, and the chain cascades through four rounds to finality 1. So the difference is not the validator count but whether a round rests at one height. The rule is a real bound — it is what stops a burst at one height enqueuing a proposal per block (#70's fan-out) — and its own comment says it depends on the height *advancing*, which is the case this one breaks. **Not a cost finding:** production is bounded and stops, unlike #148's storm; what it shares with #148 is the frozen finality. The fix is a design question (key the tap on the round rather than the height, or on the tip) and is deliberately not guessed. Falsified: `a_round_that_comes_to_rest_at_one_height_is_sealed_by_its_own_bound` runs the rule as a sequence and asserts 1 answered against 7; mutating `>` to `>=` turns it red with `left: 7, right: 1`. **Fixed 2026-10-01**: the tap is keyed per-*sender* (one request per sender per height) rather than per height, so a round that comes to rest at one height answers each peer's block and advances instead of sealing. Falsifier (inverted): `a_round_that_comes_to_rest_at_one_height_is_answered_for_every_peer`.

**the restoring rule's clearing branch is a no-op that reports success**: `restore_divergent_justifications` writes the cleared record back with `dag.insert(record, msg)`, but `revalidated_record` keeps the block's hash (`multi_parent_casper.rs:394-409`), `BlockMetadataStore::contains` is `dag_set.contains(hash)` with every hash inserted unconditionally (`block-storage/src/dag/metadata_store.rs:71`), and `dag.insert` returns `Ok(())` **without writing** when the hash is already known (`casper/src/dag.rs:322-328`). So the store keeps `validation_failed: true`, the representation is untouched, and the rule logs "cleared the failure record for ... the block validates" while doing nothing. **This is what "its clearing branch is not verified end to end" was** - not a verification gap but a path that cannot succeed, and a log that says otherwise. Invisible to `casper/tests/restoring_rule.rs` because that file drives a **fake** storage whose `insert` unconditionally records (`inserts_for`), so the real short-circuit is never in the path (C186's fixture lesson, one layer up). Found by checking the premise of #156's repair rather than by looking for it **Fixed 2026-10-01**: `BlockDagStorage::update_metadata` - the update `insert` cannot be, since it returns `Ok` without writing for a hash it holds - replaces the call at `multi_parent_casper.rs`, and it takes the block back into the height map and into `latest_msgs` through the new `DagMessageState::promote_msg_mut`. The same primitive is what C190's proposer-side self-clearing step needs, so this write path closes both rows. The no-op also made `restore_attempts` and the per-block budget inert; both are written by this path now.

**the self-equivocation #156 recorded is a proposer/sync race, not the failed record C190 named** - `proposer.rs` derives `seq_num` from a `latest_msgs` snapshot (`create_block`, `:583`) and inserts the block much later (`dag.insert`, `:432`); during LFS re-sync `populate_dag` re-inserts the node's own old block into that window, taking the `(sender, seq_num)`, so the insert's H-1 gate rejects the proposal as an equivocation. The rejection was wrapped as a generic `Internal` and counted toward `consecutive_failures`, so three of them halted the autopropose timer (#157). Reproduced on the instrumented run (§48): 11 equivocations, 1 halt, and **0** `validation failed` records - no failed record is involved, so C190's repair (which clears a `Divergence` self-record) is never reached on this tree. **Fixed 2026-10-01**: the equivocation is matched on `dag.rs`'s shared `EQUIVOCATION_PREFIX` and surfaced as `ValidateError::SelfEquivocation`; `do_propose` treats it as *not due* (`NotEnoughNewBlocks`) rather than counting it, so the next tick re-derives from the now-current DAG. The equivocation is still counted, on its own gauge (`stale_snapshot_self_equivocations`, on `/metrics` and `/api/status`), so a node that never recovers stays visible. Node-local: §6 and `#51` §A are not engaged.

**the routing layer reported a healthy proposer for ever, because it never delegated `proposer_health`** - `ShardRoutingBlockApi` implements `BlockApi` but did not override `proposer_health()`, so it fell back to the trait's all-zero default and `/api/status` answered `consecutiveSelfValidationFailures: 0`/`autoproposeTimerHalted: false` regardless of the live proposer state - the two #157 fields were broken on the status surface the whole time, invisible because 'quiet' and 'healthy' read the same. Exposed when C194's third field (`staleSnapshotSelfEquivocations`) was added beside them and the devnet showed it live on `/metrics` (12) but zero on `/api/status`. **Fixed 2026-10-01**: delegate `proposer_health()` to the primary, like `status()`; the router test now asserts the primary's marker reaches the caller rather than the default. Node-local observability, not a consensus rule.

**C171's pace bound was not scoped to the node's own proposals, so it silenced a caller's propose.** The #70 storm is a node *reacting* to remote blocks -- the attest-on-new-blocks tap and autopropose, each an attestation that is in turn a remote block for the next -- but `attestation_suppressed` applied the pace term in `create_block` for every source, so on a caught-up node with no deploy to attest to an explicit `POST /api/v1/propose` returned `NoNewDeploys` (a 400) instead of a block. That is the contract `tools/devnet.sh` states ("A block is created only when one of these fires: ... or (c) an explicit `propose`/`POST /api/v1/propose`") and `tools/devnet-test.sh` step 5 asserts (`POST /api/propose returns 200`). Found by CI on this branch: `node/tests/api_surface.rs`'s arm 2 answered 400 where the same test had passed at every earlier commit of the branch. **Fixed 2026-10-01**: provenance travels with the queued request -- `ProposeSource::Explicit` (admin HTTP, the gRPC propose service, `--propose-on-deploy`) vs `Automatic` (the autopropose tap and timer, the attest-on-new-blocks tap, and the follow-up a colliding request resolves to) -- and only an `Automatic` proposal is paced. Falsifiers: the unit `an_explicit_propose_is_not_paced_by_the_storm_bound` asserts the identical inputs the `paced` arm beside it asserts suppressed, and the node-level arm was reproduced red locally then observed green, with the exemption neutralized to confirm it is the term under test. The storm arm is unchanged: a caught-up *automatic* attestation without a deploy is still withheld.

**`slash` leaves the slashed validator's `committedRewards` entry behind, where the oracle deletes it.** The contract's slash state update removes the entry as well as zeroing the bond (`casper/src/genesis/resources/Pos.rhox`, the `stateUpdateCh!` block: `committedRewards: state.get("committedRewards").delete(slashedValidator)`), but `NativeSystemState::slash` (`rholang/src/native_state.rs:1421-1448`) edits only the pool, the active set and the two withdrawal maps. The entry is then unreachable in both directions: never paid, because `close_block` pays pool members (`:1253`) and claims in `withdrawers` (`:1281`) only and the slashed validator is out of both; and never removed, because the sole `committed.remove` is `:1291`, the claim payment. Two consensus-visible consequences: the accrued rewards are stranded in the staking vault for ever, and because `epoch_pot` subtracts every `committed` entry (`:668`) they keep reducing the distributable pot, so after any slash of a validator that had crossed a boundary the port distributes a smaller remainder than the oracle. No test covers the slash/committed interaction. Deletion matches the oracle; leaving it is the deviation. **Fixed 2026-10-02**: `NativeSystemState::slash` now removes the entry with the rest of the validator's records, so the accrued amount returns to the distributable pot — the oracle's behaviour rather than a stranded balance. **The destination changed with C199**: the entry is still cleared, but the amount is now split by the offence's tier — the tier's share to the Coop vault and the rest back to the validator — rather than dropped into the pot, because the accrued reward is part of what a slash is a share *of*.

**the offence predicate was wider than fault: three of the fourteen slashable causes read the receiving node's own configuration or version, and a disagreement about blame is a chain split rather than a tolerated divergence.** `mark_failed` set `slashable: matches!(cause, FailureCause::Attributable)`, and `Attributable` is the right test for *blame* but the wrong one for *slashing*: `ContainsLowCostDeploy` reads this node's `casper.min-phlo-price`, `TooManyJustifications` its `casper.max-number-of-parents`, and `InvalidVersion` the software's `SUPPORTED` set — and none of the three is genesis identity (`GenesisBlockData` and `PosParams` carry neither knob), so two correctly-configured operators can hold different values with no committed value to be wrong about. The consequence is not a difference of opinion: `slash_is_unjustified` (`casper/src/interpreter_util.rs:170`) refuses any block whose slashes it cannot re-derive from its own metadata, so the strict node's `Slash(X)` is a block the permissive node rejects — permanently, over a local setting, with X's whole bond confiscated. **Fixed 2026-10-02**: `BlockStatus::is_slashing_offence` (`casper/src/block_status.rs`) is the offence predicate, deliberately narrower than `Attributable`, and `mark_failed` now takes the status and derives both the cause and the offence from it. The predicate admits only the block's own signed fields, the DAG's structure and the version-coupled constants (`DEPLOY_LIFESPAN`, `MAX_BLOCK_DEPLOYS`, `MAX_BLOCK_PHLO`); the three local-input statuses are still refused and stop being offences. Hard-fork class (registry section 6, #51 category A): a proposer on a fixed node no longer includes a `Slash` an unfixed one would.

**the slash took the whole bond whatever the offence.** `mark_failed` set `slashable: matches!(cause, FailureCause::Attributable)` and `NativeSystemState::slash` moved the validator's **entire** pooled bond to the Coop vault (`pool.remove(validator)`), with no partial, no cap and no reversal — so a forged deploy and a stale one cost the same total loss, while going offline cost nothing at all. A rule with no gradation makes the worst case total and an operator's exposure unstated, which is the case the risk plan's first half exists for. **Fixed 2026-10-02**: the offence now carries a **tier**, and the tier is a share of **everything the validator holds in the PoS system** — its bond, its accrued and unwithdrawn rewards, and an escrowed withdrawal claim — with the remainder **returned to its own vault**, so the loss is exactly the tier. `BlockStatus::slash_severity` is the table (AUDIT C198's offence predicate is its `is_some`): `Malicious` = forgery, all of it; `Misdemeanour` = a rule the author's own block breaks, a quarter; `HonestMistake` = a bound a stale deploy pool or a clock skew explains, a tenth. The tier travels in the block's own `SystemDeployData::Slash`, is re-derived by every receiver from its own metadata and **checked** (`slash_is_unjustified`), so a proposer cannot size the confiscation freely; a validator that offended more than once answers for the **worst** tier it committed. `SlashSeverity::Unspecified` is code 0 — the pre-tier rule, which takes everything — so a record written before the tiers replays unchanged. The model carries the same rule (`Rchain.slash`, law 44): `slash_conserves`, `a_milder_tier_takes_no_more`, `slash_clears_every_ledger`, with `atRisk` and the three tiers.

**equivocation — the one unambiguous Byzantine fault — could be refused and never punished.** The H-1 gate rejects a second block at a `(sender, seq_num)` the DAG already holds (`casper/src/dag.rs`) and returns **before any write**, so the refused block was never stored, never became a `BlockStatus`, never reached `mark_failed`, and was never an offence: a validator could double-sign for ever at no cost, while producing a single block that another node's **local setting** refused cost it its entire bond (AUDIT C198). Two signed blocks at one sequence number is the only fault that is objective by construction — anyone can verify both — and it was the only one with no penalty at all. **Fixed 2026-10-02:** the evidence travels. The gate records the refused block's **header** (`BlockDagStorage::recorded_equivocations`, the only place the offence ever exists); the proposer folds every recorded equivocation by a **bonded** sender into its slash set at the `Malicious` tier with the evidence **attached**; and `slash_is_unjustified` accepts that arm only through `validate::equivocation_is_proved`, which re-checks it against **the receiver's own DAG** — the header must be signed by the named offender (`EquivocationEvidence::is_signed_by`) and the DAG must already hold a *different* block by that sender at that `seq_num`. Nothing is taken on the proposer's word, and forged, relabelled or non-conflicting payloads are refused. **The payload is a header, not the block**: it lands in a slashing block's own `state`, i.e. in consensus data every node stores, and a block refused at the gate has passed no check at all — so carrying the block would let any peer write an object of its own choosing into consensus state. Every field of `EquivocationEvidenceProto` is fixed-width, so the payload is a few hundred bytes whatever the offender does, and a malformed field is refused at `decode` rather than reaching the signature check. Hard fork (#51 category A): a fixed node proposes a `Slash` an unfixed one cannot, and accepts one an unfixed one refuses.

**the proposer re-nominates a `Slash` for a validator that is no longer bonded, on every block, for ever.** Found by the live A2 arm (`spec/audit/evidence/a2-live-equivocation-run.sh`, #150): the bootstrap's proposer logged `[pos] slashing 1 bonded validator(s) … Malicious/10000bps (equivocation evidence)` **59 times and still counting** at a chain height of 62 — one per block — while every one of those blocks carried a `bonds` map with the offender already gone, the transition being block 22. The evidence arm of the fold is gated on `bonded` (`casper/src/blocks/proposer/proposer.rs`, `add_recorded_equivocations`), and `bonded` is `compute_bonds(pre_state_hash)` — `pos:active` read at the pre-state — so it should exclude a validator that `slash` has removed from both the pool and the active set (`rholang/src/native_state.rs`, `active.remove(validator)`). **The observation and the reading of the code cannot both be right.** One half is now measured and clean: `a_slashed_validator_is_absent_from_the_bonds_at_the_post_state` slashes a bonded validator and asks `compute_bonds` at that block's post-state — the victim is absent, so the leaf is written and read correctly *at a post-state*. What differs in the live run is therefore **which hash the proposer reads**: the *merged* pre-state, whose native view is reconstructed from the native-changes sidecar (`MergeScope::merge`, issue #74). **Impact as far as the run shows: bounded** — the repeated slash is idempotent (the offender is already out of the pool, so `slash` confiscates nothing), both nodes replayed it identically, and the chain advanced to 62 with no disagreement. Named anyway because the read that is stale here is the proposer's own view of who is bonded, and the same read feeds `check_active_validator` and the attestation quorum — the class is why this is a row rather than a note. **Not fixed**: the diagnosis stops at `compute_bonds` at a post-state being correct, and the merge fixture that would finish it is the unit this row asks for.
column7: a **merged** pre-state fixture — the same test as `a_slashed_validator_is_absent_from_the_bonds_at_the_post_state` with a merge in the middle: build a two-parent block whose parents include a slashing block and assert the victim is absent from `compute_bonds(merged_root)`. If it passes, the stale read is in the proposer's hash choice and not in the merge; if it fails, the merge's native reconstruction (#74) is the defect and this row closes into a fix there
